n: God tells His prophet to shout like a trumpet blast and not hold back: show My people their sins. Prophets are called to speak plainly even when it’s unwelcome.

f.w: lift up thy voice like a trumpet
spare not

n: The irony: they look very religious. They seek God daily, seem eager to learn His ways, and enjoy drawing near—as if they were a righteous nation.

f.w: as a nation that did righteousness

n: They complain: “We fasted—why don’t You notice?” God answers: on your fast day you pursue your own business and drive your workers hard.

f.w: afflicted our soul
exact all your labours
f.g: Demand full work from your laborers.

n: Their fasting ends in quarrels and fistfights. Fasting like that won’t get your voice heard in heaven.

f.w: ye fast for strife and debate

n: Is that the kind of fast I want—just a day of looking miserable, bowing your head like a drooping reed, and sitting on sackcloth and ashes? Outward show isn’t the point.

f.w: bow down his head as a bulrush
f.g: Droop like a reed in the wind—a display of piety.

f.w: sackcloth and ashes

n: The fast God chooses: break the chains of injustice, lift heavy burdens, free the oppressed, and smash every yoke. True fasting changes how we treat others.

f.w: Is not this the fast that I have chosen?
to let the oppressed go free

n: Share your food with the hungry, take in the homeless poor, clothe the naked, and don’t turn away from your own relatives. Latter-day Saints practice this through the monthly fast and fast offerings for the needy.

f.w: deal thy bread to the hungry
thine own flesh

n: Then your light will dawn like morning and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go before you and the Lord’s glory will guard you from behind—like Israel’s pillar of cloud.

f.w: thy light break forth as the morning
rearward

n: Then when you call, the Lord will answer, “Here I am.” This requires removing oppression, finger-pointing, and malicious talk from among you.

f.w: he shall say, Here I am
the putting forth of the finger

n: If you give yourself to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted, your light will rise in the darkness and your gloom become like noon.

f.w: draw out thy soul to the hungry
f.g: Pour yourself out—give generously and with real feeling.

n: The Lord will guide you always, satisfy you in dry seasons, and strengthen your bones. You’ll be like a well-watered garden and a spring that never runs dry.

f.w: like a watered garden
make fat thy bones

n: Your people will rebuild ancient ruins and restore old foundations; you’ll be called “Repairer of the Breach” and “Restorer of Streets to Live In.” Latter-day Saints see in this a call to build Zion and restore what was lost.

f.w: The repairer of the breach
f.g: One who rebuilds broken walls—restoring what was broken.

f.w: build the old waste places

n: If you stop trampling the Sabbath with your own business, call it a delight, honor it, and set aside your own pursuits and idle talk on God’s holy day...

f.w: call the sabbath a delight
turn away thy foot from the sabbath
f.g: Stop treading on it—stop treating it as an ordinary day.

n: ...then you will find joy in the Lord, ride on the heights of the land, and enjoy the inheritance promised to Jacob. The Lord has spoken it.

f.w: ride upon the high places of the earth
the heritage of Jacob thy father
